studies.label: Design task: sketching vs generative AI (water-saving concept design)
studies.cluster_se_treatment: No full-sample SEs or cluster-adjusted uncertainty are reported. The only inferential comparisons are subset independent-samples t-tests using ideas as observations, without adjustment for assigned student groups or repeated ideas within students (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.1).

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; PDF p. 4, Section 3.2.2 (assignment); Section 3.2.3 repeats the analyzed arm counts
counts_source.quote: The study involved 61 industrial design bachelor students ... four student groups, randomly assigned to two predefined conditions: sketch groups A+C (n=31) and AI groups B+D (n=30).

arms.name: Sketch groups (A+C)
arms.description: Control student groups used pen and paper to sketch, with no devices or additional creative stimuli; students completed the exercise individually.

arms.name: AI groups (B+D)
arms.description: Experimental student groups freely chose LLM and text-to-image tools on their own laptops or smartphones for individual ideation and visualization; no prior prompting training was provided.

studies.task: Individually generate several concepts and detail a few to promote conscious water use in the home, documenting sketches or AI conversations and images.

ai_tool.name: Student-selected tools: ChatGPT GPT-4o free with fallback to a previous model; GPT-4o Plus; DeepSeek-R1; Copilot (Azure-hosted GPT-4-class); Gemini 2.5; Leonardo.AI (Phoenix); Krea.AI (Krea 1); Meshy.AI; Vizcom; PromeAI; ArtGuru; GenCraft.
ai_tool.locator: PDF pp. 8-9, Section 4.2.5. Tools were used in April 2025; tool release years are not printed, so year is null. LLM use was followed by text-to-image generation.

preregistration.where: No preregistration or preregistered primary outcome is stated in the full document.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Consensual Assessment Technique: five-point scale from not creative to highly creative, rated by three design professors with more than ten years of experience. Each item is an image-level concept with explanatory text; image variations of the same idea count as one concept. Experts rated independently and re-rated in reverse order. Table 1 reports the score per idea, not a participant-level average.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: subset creativity test printed as Group A (Sketch) versus Group C (AI)
not_extracted.reason: Not a full-sample contrast; each side is a subset of its condition. PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.1 prints Group A (Sketch, n = 54, M = 2.36, SD = 0.61) versus Group C (AI, n = 24, M = 2.94, SD = 0.58), t(76) = -3.995, p < .001, d = 0.60, 95% CI [-0.98, -0.47]. The n values count ideas. These group letters conflict with the assignment in Figure 1 and Section 3.2.2, and the positive d is outside its negative interval. No correction or combination of these statistics is attempted.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: subset creativity test printed as Group B (Sketch) versus Group D (AI)
not_extracted.reason: Not a full-sample contrast; each side is a subset of its condition. PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.1 prints Group B (Sketch, n = 17, M = 3.04, SD = 0.62) versus Group D (AI, n = 20, M = 2.82, SD = 0.68), t (34.8) = 1.039, p = .306. The n values count ideas, not people. The condition label for Group B conflicts with Figure 1 and Section 3.2.2; this subset test cannot supply uncertainty for the full-arm Table 1 comparison.
Pre-task assessment of creative potential, with no randomized AI-versus-comparison outcome contrast. These baseline scores are not with_ai or after_ai outcomes (PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 3.2.1 and 4.1).

open_items: PDF p. 4, Section 3.2.2 randomizes student groups, but does not identify them as teams, classes, or sessions or describe their formation or randomization procedure. assignment_unit is null because the permitted vocabulary lacks an unspecified-group code; this is a clustered design, not individual assignment. Figure 1 (PDF p. 3) and the named groups establish two groups per condition.

Participant-level creativity SDs and any full-arm precision accounting for randomized groups and repeated ideas within students are absent. No uncertainty from either subset idea-level t-test should be attached to the full-sample means (PDF p. 6, Table 1 and Section 4.2.1).

The subgroup letters in the creativity tests conflict with the assignment: Figure 1 and Section 3.2.2 use sketch A+C and AI B+D, but Section 4.2.1 labels A and B Sketch and C and D AI. Correct identities and the rationale for the paired group comparisons remain unresolved.

The subset result printed as d = 0.60, 95% CI [-0.98, -0.47] is internally inconsistent; the PDF provides no correction (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2.1). Values are retained in not_extracted as printed, not recomputed.
No SD, SE, confidence interval, or test is printed for full-sample image-level fluency, total fluency, or categories per student (PDF p. 7, Section 4.2.3).

The homogenization outcome lacks the sketch-arm count or percentage and all uncertainty (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 4.2.2-4.2.3). Category coverage has no text-printed numeric arm levels or uncertainty; Figure 5-only values are not extracted (PDF p. 8).

The diagnostic AUT range counts do not match the stated design-task sample, and the paper does not explain participant flow or when group randomization occurred relative to diagnosis (PDF pp. 3-5, Sections 3.1, 3.2.2-3.2.3, and 4.1). No task-participant exclusions are stated; exclusions from the separate prompt-log analysis do not establish exclusions from the outcome sample.
Participant country and recruitment institution are not explicitly stated. Author affiliations and local examples do not establish participant location; country remains null (PDF pp. 1, 3, and 6).
The AI tools have no printed release years. April 2025 is the study date and is not entered as the models’ release year (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 4.2.5).

No primary outcome or preregistration is identified. The two diversity outcomes assess different output levels and have opposite qualitative directions; the paper does not select between them (PDF pp. 6-8 and 11).
notes: Extracted independently by B on 2026-10-10. Read the complete markdown conversion and all PDF pages, including references; reviewed both tables and every figure. No appendix, supplement, or posted-data location is stated, and no supplement is on file for this paper. All estimate source quotes were taken from pymupdf page text. The design-task group counts at assignment match those at outcome evaluation; no participant exclusions are stated for these outcomes. The task was a supervised workshop exercise within a mandatory course, so lab_rct follows the reconciled screening decision. Students worked individually within randomized student groups; the specific cluster type is not identified, which is why assignment_unit remains null. Arm names follow the methods and Table 1. The table’s medians and rating-range percentages are retained with the creativity estimate; subset tests are inventoried in not_extracted. Numeric Figure 5 values are intentionally not transcribed. JSON uses a decimal point for the flexibility value whose original quote has a decimal comma; n_units for pooled coverage transcribes the caption’s word "two." No effects, differences, variances, counts from degrees of freedom, or figure-derived category totals were computed.
